notes: Around 2 October 2025 (as reported), the national guardsmen and the drug addiction clinic's administrator attacked a charity hospital's doctor in Novoye Devyatkino, Leningrad. The doctor of an organization that helps homeless people in the region arrived to the drug addiction clinic to deliver a patient, the clinic personnel refused to admit the patient and called the police, while the head of the medical service of the clinic punched the doctor. The national guard arrived to the scene and initially resolved the conflict peacefully, however when the doctor was leaving the premises, they've attacked him under the guise of arresting him for a hit and run. The doctor got into the car, the guardsmen broke the window, pepper sprayed the inside of a car, which caused the doctor to pass out, and later beaten him up while he was unconscious. The victim was hospitalized with heavy bruising.

Around 2 October 2025 (as reported), a man (likely a Russkaya Obshchina member) reprimanded a Dagestani MMA fighter for praying in public and brawled with him in Murino, Leningrad. The man, who was suspectedly armed with a knife, called for reinforcements, Russkaya Obshchina members arrived and performed a 'citizen's arrest' on a fighter. The fact that the members arrived so quickly led to suspicious that the whole situation was a provocation from the beginning. Both initial fighters sustained bruises.

On 9 October 2025, in La Libertad (Santa Elena), two unidentified armed assailants on a motorcycle fatally shot a man in the back in a drive-by shooting during the afternoon in Simon Bolivar neighborhood. Investigations are ongoing. 2 fatalities.

On 9 October 2025, in Milagro (Guayas), an unknown number of armed assailants on a motorcycle fatally shot two men in a drive-by shooting on Amazonas and Escobedo streets. source: Diario Extra (Ecuador); Ecuador Comunicacion; Ecuavisa; El Diario (Ecuador); Primicias
notes: On 9 October 2025, in Jaramijo (Manabi), two armed assailants entered a nightclub and fatally shot a man. Two other people were taken to the hospital and remain in stable condition. No arrests were made and investigations are ongoing. 1 fatality.

On 10 October 2025, in Valdivia (Santa Elena), residents blocked the Spondylus route with sticks and tires to protest the killing of four men on 9 October 2025 (coded separately). Demonstrators demanded increased security and a stronger police presence amid rising violence.

On 10 October 2025, in Guayaquil - Tarqui (Guayas), five unidentified armed assailants forcefully entered a house in Mucho Lote 1 and killed four men. One of the victims had prior criminal records for organized crime involvement. No arrests were made. 4 fatalities.

Around 9 October 2025 (as reported), in Sucua (Sucua, Morona Santiago), parents, teachers, and former students of the Arcesio Gonzalez Velez school held a peaceful march demanding the construction of six classrooms promised in a 2023 agreement between the Ministry of Education and the municipal government.

Around 10 October 2025 (as reported), in Quevedo canton (Los Rios), police forces rescued two victims of extortion-related kidnapping and arrested four suspects linked to the Los Choneros gang. The operation resulted in the seizure of restraints, chains, and sharp weapons.

On 9 October 2025, in La Concordia canton (Santo Domingo de los Tsachilas), armed assailants kidnapped a father and son who had gone to show land to potential buyers and held them for ransom. notes: On 8 October 2025, in Nassau, New Providence, hundreds of members of the Bahamas Public Services Union (BPSU), the Bahamas Union of Teachers (BUT) and other supporters protested in front of the House of Assembly on Bay Street, to demand an audience with the Prime Minister over salary-related issues. Protestors sat on Bay Street, prompting police officers to intervene and ask them to move, but they remained in front of the building. Two union leaders eventually entered the building and later exited with the Prime Minister, who promised that the money protestors were demanding would be paid.

On 4 October 2025, in Caye Caulker Village, Belize, residents from Caye Caulker, Belize City and Belmopan led by church leaders protested against a referendum on cannabis legalization on Caye Caulker island, calling on voters to vote against the legalization. Protestors marched through the village with signs, and ended with a rally where they sang, danced and prayed.

On 28 September 2025, in Heredia, Heredia, according to witnesses, seven police officers sexually and physically assaulted a man in a public road. In a video, the officers were seen violently assaulting the victim. The officers were detained on 6 October, although they were released a few days later. The health conditions of the victim are unknown.

On 8 October 2025, in San Jose, San Jose, a group of women held a protest showing banners in the public stalls of the Legislative Assembly reacting to the accusations of sexual abuse against an underage girl made against a deputy and presidential candidate. The protesters demanded he renounce his parliamentary immunity to face the accusations in court. The deputy is accused of having committed abuses against a 13-year-old girl around 20 years ago.

On 8 October 2025, in San Jose, San Jose, overnight, a group of rice producers held a protest in front of the Legislative Assembly to pressure the Government to expedite the approval of Bill 24,211, known as Fonarroz. The bill would establish a fund to support the national production of rice.

On 7 October 2025, in Marianao, La Habana, overnight, dozens of residents of the Santa Felicia neighborhood held a pot-banging protest and blocked a road to complain about prolonged water and electricity outages, food shortages and lack of freedoms. The police intervened to restore ordered and arrested some protesters (exact number unknown).

On 9 October 2025, in Habana, La Habana, a group of citizens, accompanied by representatives of the Government and workers of the Electric Union (UNE), held a protest in front of the US Embassy to condemn the Israeli occupation of the Palestinian territories and the Palestinian genocide and to blame the US for their support to Israel. Governmental authorities claim that more than 100,000 citizens took part in the protest, whereas independent media estimate that about 32,000 people attended the event.

On 3 October 2025, near Tabara Abajo, Azua, dozens of farmers from the Los Guiros community held a protest demanding the relocation of their lands after they were evicted from the Monte Grande rural area due to the construction of a dam. Relocation had been promised by the national government, although it never happened despite the inauguration of the dam in 2024.

On 3 October 2025, in Santo Domingo, Distrito Nacional, overnight, residents took to the streets in the Villa Consuelo and Villa Maria neighborhoods, as well as down the Francisco del Rosario Sanchez bridge (a.k.a. 'bridge of the 17') to decry power outages. Demonstrators set up barricades of burning tires and garbage. The mobilization lasted until the early hours of 4 October.

On 10 October 2025, in Santo Domingo, Distrito Nacional, members of the National Association of Agricultural Professionals (ANPA) held a protest in front of the Agriculture Ministry demanding higher salaries and pensions, among other labor-related claims. Protesters blocked the roadway at J.F Kennedy Avenue and police forces intervened to restore circulation. No interaction between the officers and the protesters was mentioned.

On 4 October 2025, in Fraijanes, Guatemala, armed men inside the Pavoncito prison stabbed and killed an MS-13 gang member. The identity of the perpetrators and the reason for the attack are unknown, however, the perpetrators are likely members of this gang since the attack occurred in an annex of Pavoncito prison in which only MS-13 gang members are detained. 1 fatality.

Around 5 October 2025 (as reported), in San Martin Sacatepequez, Quetzaltenango, two police officers under the influence of alcohol beat up a young man and threatened to report him, if he didn't pay them money (coded separately). On 8 October 2025, in Santiago Atitlan, Solola, members of the Tzutujil community, a Mayan indigenous group, who have occupied the Santiago Atitlan City Hall since 16 September to demand the dismissal of the Mayor (coded separately), exited the city hall's premises and met with police officers who were deployed to evict the protesters. The protesters engaged peacefully with the authorities, explained their reasons to protest, and subsequently held a march outside the City Hall. No violent altercations between the parties took place. Following the dialogue, the police withdrew from the area and the protesters re-occupied the city hall's premises.

Around 9 October 2025 (as reported), in El Fiscal, Guatemala, three men were killed (methods unknown) and their bodies were found wrapped in plastic bags, at km 20 of the Atlantic Route. The police suspect that the attack is linked to the discovery of an additional body in El Triunfo, located next to a written note containing intimidations (coded separately). 3 fatalities.

On 10 October 2025, in Guatemala City, Guatemala, members of the workers' union of the Ministry of Labor and Social Security (Sitramitraps) held a protest and blocked a road outside the Ministry of Labor's facilities in Zone 9 in protest against issues related to the Collecting Agreement on Working Conditions. Around 10 October 2025 (as reported), in Mixco, Guatemala, a man was shot and killed and his body was found in El Milagro, Zone 6, next to a note containing an intimidating message against extortionists and signed by the 'organized neighbors' group. The police suspect that the attack was a retaliation against extortionists in the area. 1 fatality.

Demonstrators set up barricades of burning tires and gunshots were heard. They also forced businesses and administrative institutions to close their offices.

On 29 September 2025, near Belladere, Centre, members of the population demonstrated by blocking the road between Belladere and the border with the Dominican Republic. The demonstrators also threw stones while demanding security in the country.
On 29 September 2025, in Roseaux, Grande-Anse, members of the population protested by erecting a roadblock. The motivation of the protest is unknown.
On 29 September 2025, in Limbe, Centre, members of the population marched to demand the release of an entrepreneur who was kidnapped on 9 September (coded separately).

On 29 September 2025, in Petit-Goave, Ouest, members of the population protested by erecting a roadblock. The motivation of the protest is unknown.

On 29 September 2025, in Delmas, Ouest, an unknown number of people were kidnapped on the Airport Road. Although there is no information on the perpetrators, latest reports suggest that most abductions are gang-related. The victims' whereabouts are unknown.

On 30 September 2025, in Petion Ville - Thomassin, Ouest, armed individuals kidnapped an unknown number of residents on their way to their gardens in the Boucan area. Gunshots were also heard in the area, although the circumstances are unclear. The victim(s)' whereabouts are unknown.

On 30 September 2025, in Port-au-Prince - Champs de Mars, Ouest, members of the Viv Ansanm gang opened fire on residents near the Departmental Law Enforcement Unit (UDMO) base, injuring at least two people, a vendor and a disabled person. The police intervened, causing a clash. Some residents locked themselves inside their homes while others fled the area. At least 2 injured.

On 1 October 2025, in Delmas - Village W. Lamothe, Ouest, an unknown number of people were kidnapped in Delmas 29. Although there is no information on the circumstances or perpetrators, latest reports suggest that most abductions are gang-related. The victim(s)' whereabouts are unknown.

On 2 October 2025, in Delmas - Kernizan, Ouest, members of the population demonstrated by erecting barricades of burning tires blocking the road near the Ministry of Public Works, Transport and Communications (MTPTC). They demanded the raise of the minimum wage and the reopening of the Labor and Social Security court.

Around 4 October 2025 (between 3 - 6 October), in Saint-Marc, Artibonite, residents held a protest and blocked the 'Portail des Guepes' area (Northern entry of the city) to decry gang violence. The protest was supported by multiple social and political organizations, and was part of a movement from Pont Sonde calling for the complete cessation of activities until the dismantling of the Baz Gran Grif de Savien Gang. A protest over the same claims was held in Pont Sonde on 3 October (coded separately).

On 5 October 2025, in Pont Sonde, Artibonite, residents held a protest and set up barricades along the National Road 1 demanding the dismantling of gangs and their bases. Protests on the same claims were held in Pont Sonde and Saint-Marc since 3 October (coded separately).

On 6 October 2025, in the Saint-Marc commune, Artibonite, self-defense group members supported by residents coming from Pont Sonde demonstrated and forced the closure of schools (unclear methods) in the commune as they demanded equality for students who have seen their access to education affected by the violence of gangs in areas under gang control. Following the protest, the national authorities temporarily suspended the application of the measures. The protest was part of a labor strike that was expected to end on 8 October.

On 6 October 2025, in Leogane, Ouest, in the morning, hundreds of residents held a demonstration with banners and tree branches and blocked several streets with burning tires to prevent a police armored vehicle from being transferred to Port-au-Prince. The demonstrating residents claimed that the vehicle had contributed in the fight against the 103 Zombies Gang in the commune, and they wanted to keep it.

Several people were also injured during the attack. 2 fatalities, several injured.

On 8 October 2025, in Des Granges, Nord-Ouest, the Ti Rach Gang set fire to residents' houses and kidnapped several civilians in the Des Granges locality (Desgranges communal section). The whereabouts of the victims are unknown. Casualties unknown.

source: AFP; AP; Gazette Haiti; Haiti Standard; Le Nouvelliste (Haiti); Rezo Nodwes; Vant Bef Info
notes: On 9 October 2025, in Port-au-Prince - Champs de Mars, Ouest, police forces clashed with members of the Viv Ansamn Gang near the premises of the National Palace. The clash happened while the Transitional Presidential Council and high-ranking government officials held a meeting at the palace. Two police armored vehicle were shot at, although no human casualties were mentioned. After the clashes were over, the leader of the Viv Ansanm Gang shared a social media video mocking claims that security forces had retaken control of the Champs de Mars area. There were no casualties.

Around 4 October 2025 (between 1 - 7 October), in Rio Hondo, Francisco Morazan, a man was killed after being kidnapped by unidentified individuals who demanded L30,000 in exchange for his release. According to reports, he left his home on 1 October 2025 and was later reported missing. His family received a call from his phone in which the captors requested the ransom, but the family was unable to pay due to financial hardship. His body was found on 7 October near kilometer 24 on the road to Olancho, lying face down, shirtless and without shoes. Police and forensic teams processed the scene, and investigations are underway to identify and capture the perpetrators. 1 fatality.

On 4 October 2025, outside Talanga, Francisco Morazan, residents held a demonstration to demand the construction of a pedestrian bridge, street lighting, and road repairs near kilometer 32 of the highway to Olancho, between the communities of El Tamal and Queso. Demonstrators blocked both lanes by burning tires, disrupting vehicle traffic. Police and anti-riot units arrived with armored vehicles and initially engaged in dialogue, but the situation escalated when some demonstrators threw stones and other objects at officers, prompting a confrontation and a police pursuit. At least five individuals were arrested. One demonstrator sustained a gunshot wound but fled the area. Police dispersed the demonstrators and restored traffic flow. Demonstrators warned they would resume actions if their demands remain unaddressed.

On 4 October 2025, in Catacamas, Olancho, several heavily armed men entered a cantina operating in a residence in the Ojo de Agua neighborhood and shot and killed three women. The victims were socializing during the town's patronal festival when the attackers opened fire without warning. Two of the bodies were found near the entrance, and a third was discovered in another part of the establishment during the forensic inspection. Police and agents from the Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DPI) secured the scene, and the Public Prosecutor's Office conducted the removal of the bodies. Authorities have not made any arrests. The attack is likely related to personal disputes and territorial conflicts associated with drug trafficking. 3 fatalities.

On 5 October 2025, in Las Pinuelas, Olancho, a young boy was killed and his body was found tied to a tree and with his throat slit. The victim, originally from the Rio Blanco area, was last seen hours before the discovery. He was found under conditions of extreme violence in the Las Pinuelas community. The motive for the killing is unknown. 1 fatality.

On 6 October 2025, in Choluteca, Choluteca, unidentified individuals shot and killed a man in the Sagrado Corazon neighborhood. According to police, the incident is suspected to be a gang-related score-settling, as the victim had a criminal history and was previously involved in the killing of his own brother. 1 fatality.

On 6 October 2025, in Comayagua, Comayagua, two unidentified armed individuals posing as passengers shot and killed a taxi driver while he was operating his vehicle in the Las Tejeras sector, near the iron bridge. The assailants requested a ride and, before reaching the destination, opened fire on the victim inside the taxi. After the attack, the vehicle veered off the road into a ditch. Bystanders attempted to assist the victim, who was transported to the Santa Teresa Regional Hospital, where he died from his injuries. Police arrived at the scene to begin investigations. The perpetrators fled, and no arrests have been reported. The motive is unknown. 1 fatality.

On 6 October 2025, in Sinuapa, Ocotepeque, mototaxi drivers protested by blocking the CA-4 international highway to denounce irregularities in the assignment of unit numbers. Protesters reported the existence of 'phantom' units and the cloning of registration numbers, which they argue negatively affects their work and compromises safety in the transport sector. The roadblock caused traffic disruption in both directions and long lines of vehicles.

On 8 October 2025, in Tegucigalpa, Francisco Morazan, around 200 members of the Agrarian Platform and the Coordinator of Popular Organizations of Aguan (COPA) protested in front of the Supreme Court of Justice. Protesters demanded the enforcement of a judicial order to evict the Los Cachos Gang from lands belonging to the Camarones Campesino Cooperative in Colon. Protesters denounced that the eviction order, issued by the National Jurisdiction Court for Organized Crime, has been suspended three times since December 2024, leaving more than 150 families displaced. They also accused Los Cachos Gang of carrying out armed attacks against the El Tranvio and El Chile cooperatives and clashing with police on 1 February 2025 (coded separately), injuring 11 officers. The protesters started a sit-in outside the court that persisted until 13 October.

On 8 October 2025, in El Lolo, Francisco Morazan, residents held a peaceful protest by blocking the road to demand urgent repairs to a severely damaged 3-kilometer stretch of roadway. Protesters halted the passage of vehicles, including cars, buses, and mototaxis, causing heavy traffic congestion in the area. Protesters cited the road's poor condition, worsened by recent rains, as a serious risk to both residents and transport operators. They called on the mayor of the Central District to fulfil previous promises of road repairs.

On 8 October 2025, in Olanchito, Yoro, several heavily armed men entered a man's residence and shot him multiple times, killing him at the doorstep of his home in the 4 de Enero community, sector Medio Aguan. According to local residents, the assailants arrived directly at the house and opened fire without speaking. The attackers fled in an unknown direction. The motive is unknown. 1 fatality.

They displayed banners on their vehicles with messages demanding payment and stated they will not participate in the upcoming general election logistics unless the debt is settled. Protesters stated that multiple clinics remained without medical attention due to the ongoing protest.
